claims.source: The Saccharomyces cerevisiae TLS Polζ (henceforth referred to as ScPolζ) is a four-subunit enzyme, comprised of catalytic subunit Rev3, two regulatory subunits of Rev7, and the accessory subunits Pol31 and Pol32 (Johnson et al., 2012; Makarova et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on ScPolζ structure.

claims.claim: ScPolζ lacks 3′-to-5′ proofreading exonuclease activity.
claims.source: Current evidence suggests that the error rate during ScPolζ-catalyzed replication of undamaged DNA templates is much higher than that of DNA polymerases, as it lacks 3′-to-5′ proofreading exonuclease activity (Lawrence et al., 1985a; Lawrence et al., 1985b; Huang et al., 2002; Northam et al., 2006; Zhong et al., 2006; Kochenova et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on ScPolζ enzymatic properties.

claims.claim: S. cerevisiae rev3, rev7, or pol32 mutant strains show greatly reduced spontaneous mutation frequencies.
claims.source: Consistent with this, S. cerevisiae rev3, rev7, or pol32 mutant strains show greatly reduced spontaneous mutation frequencies, driving the notion that ScPolζ promotes DNA damage-induced mutagenesis (Quah et al., 1980; Lawrence et al., 1985a; Lawrence et al., 1985b; Morrison et al., 1989; Nelson et al., 1996, Makarova and Burgers, 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on mutation frequencies in yeast mutants.

claims.claim: Rev7 enhances Rev3 catalytic efficiency by 20- to 30-fold.
claims.source: While the catalytic subunit Rev3 alone is capable of replicating damaged DNA, Rev7 enhances its catalytic efficiency by 20- to 30-fold (Quah et al., 1980; Morrison et al., 1989; Nelson et al., 1996; Makarova and Burgers, 2015) and the accessory subunits Pol31 and Pol32 further raise it by 3- to 10-fold (Johnson et al., 2012; Makarova et al., 2012), suggesting that they abet the processivity of translesion DNA synthesis by Polζ (Acharya et al., 2006; Bezalel-Buch et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on Rev7's effect on Rev3 activity.

claims.claim: Pol31 and Pol32 further raise Rev3 catalytic efficiency by 3- to 10-fold.
claims.source: While the catalytic subunit Rev3 alone is capable of replicating damaged DNA, Rev7 enhances its catalytic efficiency by 20- to 30-fold (Quah et al., 1980; Morrison et al., 1989; Nelson et al., 1996; Makarova and Burgers, 2015) and the accessory subunits Pol31 and Pol32 further raise it by 3- to 10-fold (Johnson et al., 2012; Makarova et al., 2012), suggesting that they abet the processivity of translesion DNA synthesis by Polζ (Acharya et al., 2006; Bezalel-Buch et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on Pol31 and Pol32's effect on Rev3 activity.

claims.claim: Rev7 acts as a bridge between Rev3 and Rev1.
claims.source: Indeed, Rev7 (also known as MAD2B and MAD2L2) is an adapter protein, which acts as a bridge between Rev3 and Rev1 (Haracska et al., 2001; Kikuchi et al., 2012; Pustovalova et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on Rev7's role as an adapter protein.

claims.claim: ScPolζ holoenzyme assembles into a pentameric ring-shaped structure.
claims.source: The high-resolution cryo-EM structures of ScPolζ holoenzyme have revealed that the subunits Rev3, Rev7, Pol31, and Pol32 assemble into a pentameric ring-shaped structure in which they are maintained by a chain of uninterrupted protein–protein interaction networks (Gómez-Llorente et al., 2013; Malik et al., 2020; Du Truong et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior structural studies of ScPolζ.

claims.claim: The tetrameric Shieldin complex binds single-stranded DNA (ssDNA).
claims.source: A flurry of research has documented that the tetrameric Shieldin complex – comprising REV7, SHLD1, SHLD2, and SHLD3 – binds single-stranded DNA (ssDNA), blocks 5′ end resection and homologous recombination (HR), antagonizes the recruitment of BRCA1 to the double-strand break (DSB), while facilitating non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) (Xu et al., 2015; Boersma et al., 2015; Mirman et al., 2018; Findlay et al., 2018; Gupta et al., 2018; Ghezraoui et al., 2018; Dev et al., 2018; Tomida et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2018; Noordermeer et al., 2018; Liang et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on Shieldin complex functions.

claims.claim: The Shieldin complex blocks 5′ end resection.
claims.source: A flurry of research has documented that the tetrameric Shieldin complex – comprising REV7, SHLD1, SHLD2, and SHLD3 – binds single-stranded DNA (ssDNA), blocks 5′ end resection and homologous recombination (HR), antagonizes the recruitment of BRCA1 to the double-strand break (DSB), while facilitating non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) (Xu et al., 2015; Boersma et al., 2015; Mirman et al., 2018; Findlay et al., 2018; Gupta et al., 2018; Ghezraoui et al., 2018; Dev et al., 2018; Tomida et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2018; Noordermeer et al., 2018; Liang et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on Shieldin complex functions.

claims.claim: The Shieldin complex antagonizes the recruitment of BRCA1 to the double-strand break (DSB).
claims.source: A flurry of research has documented that the tetrameric Shieldin complex – comprising REV7, SHLD1, SHLD2, and SHLD3 – binds single-stranded DNA (ssDNA), blocks 5′ end resection and homologous recombination (HR), antagonizes the recruitment of BRCA1 to the double-strand break (DSB), while facilitating non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) (Xu et al., 2015; Boersma et al., 2015; Mirman et al., 2018; Findlay et al., 2018; Gupta et al., 2018; Ghezraoui et al., 2018; Dev et al., 2018; Tomida et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2018; Noordermeer et al., 2018; Liang et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on Shieldin complex functions.

claims.claim: The N-terminus of SHLD3 interacts with REV7 using a stereotypical 'safety-belt' interaction mechanism.
claims.source: Investigations have also shown that the N-terminus of SHLD3 interacts with REV7 using a stereotypical 'safety-belt' interaction mechanism (Gupta et al., 2018; Ghezraoui et al., 2018; Dev et al., 2018; Tomida et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2018; Noordermeer et al., 2018; Liang et al., 2020; Clairmont et al., 2020; Dai et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on SHLD3-REV7 interaction.

claims.claim: Shieldin-53BP1-RIF1 counteracts DSB resection by recruiting the CST-Polα-primase complex to promote fill-in at the resected DNA ends.
claims.source: In the alternative pathway, Shieldin-53BP1-RIF1 counteracts DSB resection and subsequent repair by recruiting the CST-Polα-primase complex to promote fill-in at the resected DNA ends (Mirman et al., 2018; Mirman et al., 2022; Mirman et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on Shieldin-53BP1-RIF1 pathway.

claims.claim: Cells derived from Fanconi anemia patients carrying homozygous mutations in REV7 display hypersensitivity to DNA cross-linking agents.
claims.source: The cells derived from Fanconi anemia patients carrying homozygous mutations in REV7 display hypersensitivity to DNA cross-linking agents, accumulate chromosome breaks during S/G2 phase and increased p21 levels (Bluteau et al., 2016), revealing its critical role in providing protection against FA disease.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on REV7 mutations in Fanconi anemia patients.

claims.claim: Rev7/MAD2L2 binds to and sequesters CDH1, an activator of APC/C, thus prevents premature anaphase onset.
claims.source: Some studies have identified non-canonical functions of Rev7/MAD2L2: for example, it binds to and sequesters CDH1, an activator of APC/C, thus prevents premature anaphase onset (Listovsky and Sale, 2013; Vaisman and Woodgate, 2017; Ling et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on Rev7's role in cell cycle regulation.

claims.claim: The MRX complex in conjunction with Sae2 catalyses endonucleolytic cleavage of 5′-terminated DNA strands.
claims.source: At DSBs in S. cerevisiae, the Mre11–Rad50–Xrs2 (MRX) in conjunction with Sae2 first catalyses endonucleolytic cleavage of 5′-terminated DNA strands and then its 3′→5' exonucleolytic activity produces a short 3′-ssDNA overhang, which is followed by resection in a 5′→3′ direction by either Exo1 or Dna2–Sgs1 complex to produce long tracks of ssDNA that are critically important for HR (Cejka and Symington, 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on MRX complex function.

claims.claim: The MRX complex's 3′→5' exonucleolytic activity produces a short 3′-ssDNA overhang.

claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on MRX complex function.

claims.claim: Shieldin orthologs are absent in yeast, fruit fly, nematode worm, zebrafish, and frog.
claims.source: Surprisingly, however, Shieldin orthologs are absent in different organisms such as yeast, fruit fly, nematode worm, zebrafish, and frog (Setiaputra and Durocher, 2019), raising the crucial question whether the Rev7-mediated regulation of DSB repair pathway choice is evolutionarily conserved in the single-cell eukaryotic organisms such as S. cerevisiae.

results.result: Rev7 physically interacts with all three MRX subunits (Mre11, Rad50, Xrs2) with sub-micromolar affinity, independently of Rev3 and endogenous MRX subunits. The interactions show positive cooperativity and are specific, as Rev7 does not bind Sae2.
results.evaluation: Multiple orthogonal assays (Y2H in different genetic backgrounds and MST with purified proteins) consistently demonstrate Rev7-MRX interactions. The Kd values (0.16-0.58 μM) are well-characterized with appropriate controls (Rev1 positive control, Sae2/eGFP negative controls). The independence from Rev3 and endogenous MRX is demonstrated through genetic experiments in deletion strains.

results.result: The C-terminal 42-amino acid segment (residues 203-245) of Rev7 is necessary and sufficient for binding to MRX subunits, while the N-terminal HORMA domain is dispensable. AlphaFold-Multimer modeling identifies specific residues mediating these interactions.
results.evaluation: Y2H data with systematic truncations clearly map the binding region to the C-terminal 42 residues. Western blots confirm comparable expression of truncated variants, ruling out expression artifacts. The sufficiency of the 42-residue peptide is demonstrated by Y2H. However, there is a discrepancy: AlphaFold models suggest residues outside the 42-aa fragment contribute to binding, which conflicts with Y2H results. MST data show Rev7-C1 has reduced but detectable affinity, partially supporting the modeling predictions.

results.result: Rev7-C1 (lacking the C-terminal 42 residues) binds MRX subunits with 3- to 8.8-fold reduced affinity compared to full-length Rev7.
results.evaluation: MST measurements provide quantitative binding data showing reduced but measurable affinity of Rev7-C1 for MRX subunits. This result is internally consistent and helps reconcile the Y2H data (which showed no interaction) with the AlphaFold predictions (which suggested additional binding residues outside the 42-aa fragment).

results.result: The Rev7 C-terminal 42-residue peptide protects cells from G-quadruplex DNA-HU-induced toxicity. rev7Δ and rev7-C1 strains are hypersensitive to HU when harboring G-quadruplex-forming motifs, while cells expressing the 42-aa peptide show robust growth.
results.evaluation: Cell viability assays clearly demonstrate differential sensitivity to HU+G4 DNA across strains. The rescue by the 42-aa peptide but not Rev7-C1 is consistent with the binding data. Controls without G4 motifs or without HU show no differential sensitivity, supporting specificity. The functional relevance of the Rev7-MRX interaction is established.

results.result: Full-length Rev7 inhibits both exonuclease and endonuclease activities of Mre11 in a dose-dependent manner, while Rev7-C1 shows reduced inhibitory activity. Rev7 does not inhibit Sae2 nuclease activity, demonstrating specificity.
results.evaluation: In vitro nuclease assays with purified proteins demonstrate dose-dependent inhibition of Mre11 by Rev7. Appropriate controls (Rev7 alone, Sae2 as specificity control) are included. The reduced activity of Rev7-C1 is consistent with its reduced binding affinity. The mechanistic link between Rev7-MRX binding and functional inhibition is established.

results.result: Rev7 inhibits Rad50's ATPase activity in a dose-dependent manner without affecting ATP binding. Rev7-C1 shows threefold reduced inhibitory activity. Rev7 does not affect Dmc1 ATPase activity, demonstrating specificity.
results.evaluation: Multiple complementary assays (UV crosslinking for ATP binding, TLC and colorimetric assays for ATP hydrolysis) consistently show Rev7 inhibits Rad50 ATPase without affecting ATP binding. Dmc1 serves as an appropriate specificity control. The reduced activity of Rev7-C1 correlates with reduced binding affinity. The data are internally consistent across different assay methods.

results.result: Rev7 promotes NHEJ in S. cerevisiae. rev7Δ shows a 4- to 9-fold decrease in NHEJ efficiency in plasmid-based and chromosomal assays. The 42-aa peptide fully restores NHEJ efficiency, while Rev7-C1 does not. The effect is independent of cell cycle defects.
results.evaluation: Two independent NHEJ assays (plasmid-based and suicide-deletion) show consistent results. Appropriate genetic controls (mre11Δ, ku70Δ) and epistasis analysis with rev1Δ and rev3Δ are included. FACS analysis rules out cell cycle artifacts. The rescue by the 42-aa peptide but not Rev7-C1 is consistent with the binding and functional data. Statistical analysis is appropriate with multiple replicates.

results.result: Rev7 suppresses homologous recombination by inhibiting Mre11-mediated short-range DNA end resection. rev7Δ shows an 11.5-fold increase in HR frequency and increased ssDNA formation at 0.7 kb (but not 3 kb) from DSBs. The 42-aa peptide, but not Rev7-C1, suppresses HR.
results.evaluation: Multiple assays (plasmid-chromosome recombination, qPCR-based resection assay) consistently demonstrate Rev7's anti-recombinogenic role. The distance-dependent effect on resection (increased at 0.7 kb but not 3 kb) specifically implicates Mre11-mediated short-range resection. Controls with mre11 nuclease-dead mutants and G4 motif mutations support the mechanism. The rescue by 42-aa peptide is consistent with other functional data.

results.result: Prior work establishes that the Shieldin complex (REV7, SHLD1-3) facilitates NHEJ while blocking HR in human cancer cells, but SHLD1-3 orthologs are absent in many eukaryotic species including S. cerevisiae.
results.evaluation: These claims accurately summarize well-established prior work with appropriate citations. The absence of Shieldin orthologs in yeast provides the biological rationale for investigating alternative mechanisms of Rev7 function.

results.result: Background claims about TLS polymerases, Polζ structure and function, Shieldin complex functions, MRX complex activities, and Rev7's roles in various cellular processes based on prior literature.
results.evaluation: These claims accurately represent established knowledge from the cited literature and provide appropriate context for the current study. They are supported by extensive citations to prior work.

results.result: Rev7 physically interacts with individual MRX subunits (Mre11, Rad50, Xrs2) as demonstrated by yeast two-hybrid assays and microscale thermophoresis, with dissociation constants in the submicromolar range. The interaction is independent of Rev3 and endogenous MRX subunits.
results.evaluation: Multiple reviewers acknowledge the interaction data as convincing. Reviewer 1 states 'the results convincingly showed that the individual subunits of MRX interacts robustly with Rev7.' The editor notes 'important data providing evidence' for the interaction. No reviewer challenges the core interaction findings from Y2H and MST experiments.

results.result: The C-terminal 42 amino acid region of Rev7 is necessary and sufficient for interaction with MRX subunits, while the N-terminal HORMA domain is dispensable. AlphaFold modeling supports these interaction interfaces.
results.evaluation: The editor explicitly states the manuscript provides 'evidence that a 42 amino acid region of Rev7 is necessary and sufficient for interaction with the Rad50-Mre11-Xrs2 complex.' Reviewer 1 notes 'the new two hybrid data showing that the 42 amino acid segment interacts with MRN are valuable,' though raises a minor question about which subunit the 42 aa segment binds in the Y2H system.

results.result: Rev7-C1 (lacking the 42 aa C-terminal region) binds to MRX subunits with reduced affinity compared to full-length Rev7 (3-fold for Mre11, 8.8-fold for Rad50, 5.6-fold for MR complex).
results.evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly requests 'The authors should also analyze if Rev7-C1 is indeed deficient in interaction with MR individually and with complex using MST assay,' indicating the data on Rev7-C1 binding affinity was added in revision but may not fully address concerns about the functional significance of this truncation.

results.result: The 42-residue C-terminal peptide of Rev7 protects cells from HU-induced toxicity when G-quadruplex-forming motifs are present, while rev7Δ and rev7-C1 strains are sensitive to this condition.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'the 42 aa peptide alone suppressed this phenotype' in the context of HU/G4 sensitivity. While Reviewer 2 initially raised concerns about the G4 connection, after revision they state 'I am satisfied with the revision. Specifically, (i) the elimination of the G4 part...significantly improved the clarity of the work.'

results.result: Full-length Rev7 inhibits Mre11 nuclease activity (both exonuclease on dsDNA and endonuclease on ssDNA) in a dose-dependent manner, while Rev7-C1 shows reduced inhibition. Rev7 does not inhibit Sae2 nuclease activity.
results.evaluation: The editor states 'Rev7 inhibits...the Mre11 nuclease' and notes 'convincing data largely support the conclusions.' Reviewer 1 acknowledges the nuclease inhibition data but raises methodological concerns about divalent cations and notes 'The use of Sae2 associated nuclease activity as a specificity control is problematic' due to debate about Sae2's intrinsic nuclease activity, though accepts it may still be useful as a control.

results.result: Rev7 inhibits Rad50 ATPase activity in a dose-dependent manner without affecting ATP binding. Rev7-C1 shows reduced inhibition compared to full-length Rev7. Rev7 does not affect Dmc1 ATPase activity.
results.evaluation: The editor states 'Rev7 inhibits...Rad50 ATPase' and the data are described as 'convincing.' Reviewer 1 notes 'The addition of Dmc1 as a specificity control for the ATPase inhibition is nice and shows a specific effect.' Reviewer 3 initially requested additional controls for ATPase specificity, which were addressed in revision.

results.result: Rev7 promotes NHEJ as demonstrated by plasmid-based and chromosomal 'suicide-deletion' assays. The rev7Δ mutant shows a 4-9 fold decrease in NHEJ efficiency, while the 42 aa peptide fully restores NHEJ to wild-type levels and Rev7-C1 shows intermediate defects.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 states 'the authors provide strong evidence that Rev7 affects NEHJ, showing a four-fold reduction in this assay' and notes 'The conclusion that Rev7 supports NHEJ mainly through the 42 aa region was validated using a chromosomal NHEJ assay.' The editor acknowledges the data support Rev7's role in NHEJ. Reviewer 3's initial concerns about cell cycle defects were addressed with FACS data.

results.result: Rev7 suppresses homologous recombination between plasmid and chromosomal ura3 alleles containing G4 structures. The rev7Δ mutant shows an 11.5-fold increase in HR frequency, while the 42 aa peptide and Rev7-C1 both suppress HR to wild-type levels.
results.evaluation: The editor notes 'the effect of Rev7 on homologous recombination is less well documented' and states 'the result that the Rev7 C-terminal truncation lacking the 42 amino acid region still suppresses homologous recombination is unexpected and unexplained.' Reviewer 1 similarly notes this result is 'unexpected and unexplained' and states 'the context appears to be system-specific and the conclusion that Rev7 abolished HR repair of DSBs is unwarranted and overly broad.' Reviewer 2 was satisfied after revision but initially raised major concerns about the G4-based HR assay.

results.result: Rev7 suppresses HR by inhibiting Mre11-mediated short-range DNA end resection. The rev7Δ rad51Δ cells show increased ssDNA at 0.7 kb from the DSB but comparable resection at 3 kb compared to controls.
results.evaluation: The editor states 'the observed effect on resection is moderate.' Reviewer 2 notes that after revision 'the implementation of the HO-endonuclease resection assay...strengthened the conclusion about the Rev7 interference with DNA resection,' indicating initial concerns were partially addressed. However, the moderate effect and the unexpected behavior of Rev7-C1 in HR assays (which still suppresses HR despite reduced MRX binding) create uncertainty about the mechanistic interpretation.

comparisons.comparison: Perfect agreement on Rev7-MRX interaction claims (C3, C28-C43, C47). Both evaluations find the Y2H and MST data convincing and well-controlled. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative Kd values and orthogonal assays; peer reviewers describe results as 'convincingly showed' the interaction. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on 42-aa binding region mapping (C4, C48-C58). Both find the Y2H truncation data convincing. OpenEval notes a discrepancy with AlphaFold predictions; peer reviewers raise a minor question about which specific subunit binds the 42-aa segment. Both rate as SUPPORTED despite minor concerns.

Disagreement on Rev7-C1 MST data (C44-C46). OpenEval finds the reduced affinity data internally consistent and helpful for reconciling Y2H with modeling (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers express uncertainty, with Reviewer 3 requesting this analysis, suggesting the data may not fully address functional significance concerns (UNCERTAIN).

Agreement on HU+G4 sensitivity assays (C59-C63). Both find the differential sensitivity data and rescue by 42-aa peptide convincing. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate controls; peer reviewers note initial concerns about G4 connection were resolved in revision. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on Mre11 nuclease inhibition (C66-C74, with C6 only in OpenEval). Both find the in vitro nuclease data convincing. OpenEval emphasizes dose-dependence and controls; peer reviewers raise methodological concerns about divalent cations and Sae2 as a control but still accept the conclusions. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on Rad50 ATPase inhibition (C76-C84, with C7-C8 only in OpenEval). Both find the data convincing with appropriate specificity controls. OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary assays; peer reviewers specifically praise the Dmc1 control added in revision. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on NHEJ role (C88-C102). Both find the plasmid and chromosomal NHEJ assays convincing with appropriate controls. OpenEval emphasizes epistasis analysis and FACS controls; peer reviewers describe evidence as 'strong' with four-fold reduction. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on homologous recombination effects (C104-C111). OpenEval finds the anti-recombinogenic data well-supported by multiple assays (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers find the effect 'less well documented' and note the Rev7-C1 result is 'unexpected and unexplained,' with concerns about system-specificity and overly broad conclusions (UNCERTAIN).

Disagreement on resection data (C112-C114). OpenEval finds the distance-dependent resection effects convincing with appropriate controls (SUPPORTED as part of R8). Peer reviewers note the effect is 'moderate' and express uncertainty about mechanistic interpretation given unexpected Rev7-C1 behavior (UNCERTAIN).
